Discord has three APIs. The REST API handles actions such as sending a
message, listing channels, or fetching history. The Gateway API pushes
real-time events over a websocket. The Voice API streams audio over UDP.

The REST API needs a bot token from the [Discord Developer
Portal](https://discord.com/developers/applications):

1.  Create an application.
2.  Under “Bot”, add a bot and copy its token.
3.  Under “OAuth2”, generate an invite URL with the `bot` scope and the
    permissions the bot needs, and open it to invite the bot to your
    server.

[`DiscordClient`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/cordslite/core.html#discordclient)
wraps an `httpx2` client with Discord’s base URL
(`https://discord.com/api/v10`) and the auth header set.

### DiscordClient

``` python
def DiscordClient(
    token:NoneType=None, # Bot token, defaulting to `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`
    user_token:NoneType=None, # User token, defaulting to `DISCORD_USER_TOKEN`. Used by `use_user=True` calls, and by every call when there is no bot token
    name:str='cordslite', # Client name for the User-Agent header
    ver:str='0.1', # Client version for the User-Agent header
):
```

*Async client for Discord’s REST API*

[`DiscordClient`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/cordslite/core.html#discordclient)
reads `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` from the environment when it gets no token.
Tokens are stripped of surrounding whitespace, since a pasted token
often carries a trailing newline, and a blank token counts as absent.

``` python
dc = DiscordClient()
```

``` python
pasted = DiscordClient(token=' abc\n', user_token='\txyz ')
test_eq((pasted.token, pasted.user_token), ('abc', 'xyz'))
test_is(DiscordClient(token='x', user_token=' \n').user_token, None)
```

## REST endpoints

Every REST call goes through `_req`. On `429 Too Many Requests` it waits
for `Retry-After` seconds and retries. Any other non-2xx response raises
[`DiscordError`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/cordslite/core.html#discorderror)
with Discord’s error code, message, and HTTP status.

*Common base class for all non-exit exceptions.*

Discord’s REST endpoints return JSON with many fields.
[`DiscordObject`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/cordslite/core.html#discordobject)
wraps the raw dict instead of declaring a property per field. Fields
read as `obj.name` or `obj['name']`. `__dir__` lists them for tab
completion in notebooks. New fields Discord adds are available without a
code change.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/cordslite/blob/main/cordslite/core.py#L65"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
):
```

*`dict` subclass that also provides access to keys as attrs, and has a
pretty markdown repr*

Discord’s hierarchy is guild, channel, message. A guild (server)
contains channels. A channel contains messages. Each level has its own
REST endpoints:

- `GET /guilds/{id}`
- `GET /guilds/{id}/channels`
- `GET /channels/{id}/messages`
- `POST /channels/{id}/messages`

[`Guild`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/cordslite/core.html#guild),
[`Channel`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/cordslite/core.html#channel),
and
[`Message`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/cordslite/core.html#message)
subclass
[`DiscordObject`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/cordslite/core.html#discordobject)
and add a `__repr__`.

Discord returns messages newest first. `messages` reverses them so the
table reads in chronological order. Reading message content needs the
`MESSAGE_CONTENT` privileged intent, enabled in the Developer Portal.
Without it, `content` is empty for messages that neither come from the
bot nor mention it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/cordslite/blob/main/cordslite/core.py#L172"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

`send` posts a JSON body. `reply_id` makes the message a reply to an
existing one. With files it switches to `multipart/form-data`: Discord
expects the message JSON in a `payload_json` field and one `files[n]`
field per file.

[`Attachment`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/cordslite/core.html#attachment)
wraps a message attachment as a
[`DiscordObject`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/cordslite/core.html#discordobject),
with `filename`, `size`, `content_type`, and `url` as attributes.
`fetch` downloads the file through the client’s `httpx2` session.

A DM is an ordinary channel in Discord’s API. `create_dm` posts to
`/users/@me/channels` with a `recipient_id` and returns a standard
[`Channel`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/cordslite/core.html#channel).
`send` and `messages` work on it unchanged. In gateway events a DM
message has no `guild_id`. A handler can tell DMs from guild messages by
that missing field.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/cordslite/blob/main/cordslite/core.py#L296"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### DiscordClient.create_dm

``` python
async def create_dm(
    user_id
):
```

``` python
dm = await dc.create_dm('346450717025894400')
await dm.send('Hello from DMs!')
```

``` python
Message(id=1549136531430580245, author='share2self', content='Hello from DMs!')
```

Reading a person’s own DMs needs that person’s account token, not a
bot’s.
[`DiscordClient`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/cordslite/core.html#discordclient)
reads `DISCORD_USER_TOKEN` from the environment, or takes `user_token`.
With no bot token it authenticates every request as the user. With both,
a call passes `use_user=True` to send the user token for that request.
Discord’s terms forbid automating a user account, so keep this to
reading your own messages, and expect the token to change when the
password does.

`dms` lists the account’s open DM channels from `/users/@me/channels`,
which is empty for a bot. A DM (type 1) has no `name` and one recipient.
A group DM (type 3) can have a `name` and several.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/cordslite/blob/main/cordslite/core.py#L302"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### DiscordClient.dms

``` python
async def dms():
```

*The account’s open DM and group DM channels; needs a user token*

``` python
dms = await dc.dms()
assert all(d.type in (ChannelType.DM, ChannelType.GROUP_DM) for d in dms)
dm = first(d for d in dms if d.type==ChannelType.DM)
test_eq(dm.url, f'{DISCORD_WEB}/@me/{dm.id}')
len(dms), len(dm.recipients)
```

    (205, 1)

``` python
dmsgs = await dm.messages(3, use_user=True)
assert all(m.channel_id==dm.id for m in dmsgs)
assert dmsgs[0].url.startswith(f'{DISCORD_WEB}/@me/{dm.id}/')
len(dmsgs)
```

    3

``` python
test_eq((await dc.channel(dm.id, use_user=True)).id, dm.id)
```

`search` and `search_all` on a DM call `/channels/{id}/messages/search`,
which only a user token can reach, so they send it without being asked.
On a guild channel they delegate to the guild as before.

``` python
found = await dm.search(limit=2)
assert all(m.channel_id==dm.id for m in found)
len(found)
```

    2

A user is a global Discord account. A member is a user within one guild,
with guild-specific data such as nickname, roles, and join date.
`nick or user['username']` shows the server nickname when set and the
global username otherwise. The members endpoint needs the
`GUILD_MEMBERS` privileged intent, enabled in the Developer Portal.

A webhook lets an external service post to a channel without a bot
token. Executing one needs only its `id` and `token`.
[`Webhook`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/cordslite/core.html#webhook)
wraps it.
[`Channel.webhooks`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/cordslite/core.html#channel.webhooks)
and
[`Guild.webhooks`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/cordslite/core.html#guild.webhooks)
list them. The webhook has `edit`, `delete`, and `send`. `send` passes
`?wait=true`. Discord then returns the created message. It accepts
per-message `username` and `avatar_url` overrides.

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/cordslite/blob/main/cordslite/core.py#L501"
